validity.recommendation: Do not add a confirming ref to Length=231km/Capacity=950 MMcf/d as-is. Re-derive this segment's length/capacity against GulfPub's whole-system figure (196 km / 500 MMcf/d Obaiyed→Ameriya) and OGJ's original 1996 design figures (315 km total, ~465 MMcf/d combined), or get an EGAS/GASCO capacity table. Also review whether the 3-way GEM segmentation (P0474 Obaiyed–Tarek 49.5km + P3934 Tarek–Ameryia 231km + P6687 Obaiyed Spurline 41.5km = 322km total) over-counts length relative to the independently-sourced 196km end-to-end route.
validity.researcher_notes: The corridor and system genuinely exist — this is not a phantom pipeline — but the specific numbers staged for this ProjectID are not corroborated and materially conflict with the two hard-numbered independent sources found. (1) The gem.wiki page's ONLY citation for Capacity/Length/Diameter/Location on ALL THREE segments (P0474, P3934, P6687) is a single reused footnote [3] (backlinks=15) to https://egyptoil-gas.com/reports/the-western-desert-egypts-giant-petroleum-reservoir/ ('The Western Desert: Egypt's Giant Petroleum Reservoir', Egypt Oil & Gas, 4 Mar 2020). Fetched that page directly: the rendered/visible body text contains ZERO occurrences of 'pipeline', 'Obaiyed', 'Tarek', 'Ameryia/Ameriya/Amreya', '950', or '231' — it is a Research & Analysis premium report whose substantive text is gated (only title/boilerplate/nav rendered). It cannot be shown to support any of these specific figures; it is a generic, unverifiable citation reused across 15 footnote instances on the wiki page, exactly the pattern that should not count as corroboration. (2) Independent trade source Oil & Gas Journal, 'Egypt western desert activity hits high gear' (4 Nov 1996): describes ONE 315 km gas pipeline from Shell's Obaiyed concession to a 640 MW power plant at Ameriya, picking up Khalda-concession (Repsol/Apache) gas en route, entering service 1999, combined design capacity ~465 MMcf/d (300 MMcf/d Shell/Obaiyed + 165 MMcf/d Repsol/Apache/Khalda). No 'Tarek' node and no diameter given — this describes the ORIGINAL single-line system before any GEM-style 3-way segmentation. (3) Independent GulfPub PE World Map (Dec-2025 SDE scrape) carries a single feature 'Western Desert Gas Project - North Line': Obaiyed field, Egypt -> Ameriya Refinery, Egypt, with an explicit note 'System is also known as the Northern Gas Pipeline and runs from the Obaiyed Field to the Amreya Refinery' — unambiguously the SAME named system as this GEM entry. GulfPub gives: length 196 km, diameter 34 in, capacity 500 MMcf/d, operator Badr El Din Petroleum Company (BAPETCO), status operating. Diameter (34in) matches GEM's P3934 exactly — supports that P3934 is at least tracking the correct trunk diameter. But GulfPub's length for the WHOLE Obaiyed→Ameriya route (196 km) is shorter than GEM's P3934 ALONE (231 km, just the middle third of GEM's 3-segment split), and GEM's 3-segment total (322 km) is 64% longer than GulfPub's single measured route (196 km). GulfPub's whole-system capacity (500 MMcf/d) is also little more than half of P3934's standalone capacity claim (950 MMcf/d), and less than double OGJ's original 1996 combined design figure (465 MMcf/d) — 950 for one interior segment looks inflated relative to both independent sources. Existence of the named waypoint 'Tarek' is real and corroborated (Egypt Oil & Gas, 'Khalda Powers Tarek Wells with 22 kV Project', names Khalda Petroleum Company's Tarek wells in the Western Desert; GulfPub separately carries a 'Western Desert Gas Project - Tarek Spur' lateral, Ras Kanayes 4 field -> Tarek field, operator KPC/Khalda) — so the segmentation concept (a Tarek junction distinct from Obaiyed and Ameriya) is plausible, but the specific 231 km / 950 MMcf/d attributed to just this middle stretch is unsupported and likely overstated. Net: real pipeline system, correctly classified (gas transmission, operating), but the length and capacity values on this specific ProjectID fail the 2-independent-source spec check and should not get a confirming ref as-is.

validity.recommendation: Change Owner from 'General Petroleum Co' (100%) to Badr El Din Petroleum Company (BAPETCO) and/or Khalda Petroleum Company (KPC) — or at minimum add Apache Corp / Shell as operator — pending human confirmation; keep Owner blank-with-note if uncertain rather than leaving an unsupported single 100% owner.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's own gem.wiki page contradicts the staged Owner value: the page's 'Background' section states the system 'was owned jointly by Apache Corporation and Shell' (as of 2004), and lists Operator as 'Apache Corporation and Shell' for the upstream Obaiyed-Tarek segment, yet lists Owner as 'General Petroleum Company (GPC)' for all three segments including this one, with no operator listed for P3934 itself. Independently, GulfPub's matching 'Western Desert Gas Project - North Line' feature (Obaiyed->Ameriya, same system) names the operator as Badr El Din Petroleum Company (BAPETCO) — the Shell/Apache-EGPC joint venture for this Western Desert concession — not General Petroleum Company. Separately, Egypt Oil & Gas trade press ('Khalda Powers Tarek Wells...') confirms the Tarek wells feeding this corridor are operated by Khalda Petroleum Company (KPC, the Apache-EGPC JV), a different EGPC-linked entity again. General Petroleum Company (GPC) is a real, distinct EGPC subsidiary but its documented concessions are concentrated in the Gulf of Suez/Eastern Desert/Sinai, not this specific Matruh/Khalda corridor, so GPC-as-sole-100%-owner is not corroborated by any independent source found; BAPETCO/Khalda/Apache/Shell are the names that actually recur across independent sources for this system.

routes.start_name: Tarek gas field / junction (Khalda concession complex, Western Desert)

waypoints.name: Obaiyed gas field, Matruh Governorate (upstream origin of the wider Northern Gas Pipeline system)

routes.corridor_desc: Part of the 'Northern Gas Pipeline' / 'Western Desert Gas Project - North Line' corridor running from the Obaiyed gas field area (Matruh Governorate, northern Western Desert, Khalda/BAPETCO concession complex) roughly east-northeast across the Western Desert, picking up Khalda-concession gas near Tarek/Ras Kanayes, and terminating at the Amreya industrial/refinery area on the southwestern edge of Alexandria Governorate. I could not source precise coordinates for Obaiyed field or the Tarek junction from any independent, verifiable source (only qualitative geologic descriptions, e.g. 'largest Jurassic gas/condensate field in the northern Western Desert... western flank of the Matruh basin' from a SEG/AAPG abstract) — leaving those lat/lon null rather than inventing points. Amreya's coordinates are corroborated via Wikipedia (city, ~30.849N 29.612E) which is consistent with, though not identical to, the Amreya refinery's own published siting further north near the coast (~31.01N 29.84E per a third-party energy-infrastructure database) — both are within the same Amreya industrial cluster southwest of Alexandria. Given the length/capacity dispute above, treat this corridor suggestion as bounding the general Western-Desert-to-Amreya routing shared by the whole 3-segment system, not a precise fix for where the Obaiyed-Tarek/Tarek-Ameryia split point falls.
routes.researcher_notes: Only the Ameriya/Amreya endpoint could be sourced to a defensible coordinate; the Western Desert (Obaiyed/Tarek) end and the precise segment boundary point are not independently pinpointable from public sources found in this pass, so no coordinates are given for them (left null) rather than fabricated. Suggested accuracy is 'low' given both the coordinate gap and the unresolved length/capacity dispute over what exactly this segment covers.

summary: P3934 (Tarek–Ameryia, part of the Obaiyed-Amreya Northern Gas Pipeline system) is a real, correctly-classified operating gas transmission trunk, but its only wiki citation is a generic, content-gated egyptoil-gas.com report reused 15x that names none of the specifics, and its Length (231km)/Capacity (950 MMcf/d) materially conflict with two independent sources (OGJ 1996: 315km/~465 MMcf/d total system; GulfPub PE World Map: 196km/500 MMcf/d for the same Obaiyed→Ameriya 'North Line', diameter matching at 34in) — do not add a confirming ref to the current numbers; also flag Owner='General Petroleum Co' against independent BAPETCO/Khalda/Apache/Shell attribution.
